WhyNotTested: A one-line getter of a cmdlet parameter that takes no pipeline input. WhyNotTested: The two unvisited points are statements after ThrowTerminatingError: the return that follows the call in the branch of a named null, and the closing brace of the catch block that reports a bad named value. Cmdlet.ThrowTerminatingError never returns, it ends the command by throwing, so nothing after it can run. The return stays because the C# compiler does not know that the call does not return; without it, a method that did return would fall into the conversion below with a null. Both branches are tested: a bad named value and a named null each end the command with InvalidParameterValue, and the tests read that error.
ResidualRisk: None: the statements cannot run while ThrowTerminatingError throws.
RelatedTests: ParameterSets.Access.Tests and ParameterSets.Audit.Tests: A bad value named on the command line; A named $null is a terminating error.

WhyNotTested: The unvisited points are the last catch (Exception) of the per-item loop, taken when the DACL API fails with anything but access denied after the item was found. A read or write of the DACL on local NTFS either succeeds or fails with access denied (covered), and the probes found no other failure for these cmdlets: an unresolvable SID is accepted, a locked file does not matter because the security APIs ignore share modes, and a dangling junction is read as the link itself. One input does trigger that catch, a deny entry without rights, which .NET refuses with an ArgumentException; Add-NTFSAccess, Remove-NTFSAccess and Add-NTFSAudit take it and are tested (an Allow entry without rights is accepted, because the module adds Synchronize to it).         A cmdlet that has no rights parameter, such as the read and inheritance cmdlets, has no such input. A second trigger exists for the cmdlets that add entries: an ACL that is full. In both editions the 1,818th entry that was added to a security descriptor in memory, with -SecurityDescriptor, raised an OverflowException, "Length of the access control list exceed the allowed maximum" (probe p37: unresolvable SIDs with ReadData; 1,816 entries were written and read back without an error, and one more added with -Path succeeded, so the overflow itself was not run with -Path). By reading the source, the -Path loop takes that exception in the same handler as the zero-mask case, whereas the -SecurityDescriptor sets have no handler around the add, so there the exception ends the cmdlet. It was not turned into a test of its own. A volume without ACL support or a corrupt descriptor cannot be created safely on the shared host.
ResidualRisk: Low: one WriteError(exception, id, category, path) and continue, the shape that the access-denied and ReadFileError siblings of the same loops assert and that the zero-mask tests assert for the cmdlets that add and remove entries. The catches of the cmdlets that only read or change inheritance have no known trigger. A catch that wraps the write of the result is entered also when a later command raises something while it takes the object; every catch-all whose try block writes directly passes that exception on (a scan of the source finds no exception; it cannot see a write inside a helper such as the owner restore of InvokeAsOwner, an accepted limitation), and the PipelineControl tests run that part for every cmdlet.
RelatedTests: Access.Tests and Audit.Tests: a deny or audit entry without rights for Add-NTFSAccess, Remove-NTFSAccess and Add-NTFSAudit (AddAceError and RemoveAceError, ArgumentException, WriteError, target, continuation, nothing written). PathErrors: ReadFileError, ReadSecurityError, denied write and ownership retry, each with continuation. PipelineControl.Tests: a break, a continue, Select-Object -First, a throw, and an error with -ErrorAction Stop after the first object.

WhyNotTested: Four groups of points. (1) The last catch (Exception) of the per-item loop, taken when the read fails with anything but access denied after the item was found: a read of the descriptor on local NTFS either succeeds or fails with access denied (covered), and the probes found no other failure (the explanation of ACCESS-GENERIC-CATCH and EFFECTIVE-ACCESS-CATCH of the 2026-10-10 report, unchanged). (2) Since rc9 (Decision 27, item 7) the catch of the ownership retry holds the check IsFromLaterCommand(ex2) with a rethrow. The rethrow runs only when a later command throws for the RestoreOwnerError record that InvokeAsOwner writes while it gives the owner back. InvokeAsOwner starts with FileSystemOwner.GetOwner, which needs the READ_CONTROL right whose denial started the retry, so the retry of a getter ends at that first statement with a ReadSecurityError and never reaches the restore: no state of an item takes a getter to the rethrow, with a local volume or a share (Decision 27, item 7: 9 of the 17 handlers have no test for this reason, the audit cmdlets for the reason of AUDIT-OWNER-RETRY). The check is the same IsFromLaterCommand call that the eight handlers with a test run. (3) GetInheritance only: the guards if (inheritanceInfo != null), in the loop of the paths and in the loop of the descriptors. Both overloads of FileSystemInheritanceInfo.GetFileSystemInheritanceInfo end in return new, so the else side of the guards has no input. (4) GetSecurityDescriptor only: it is not one of the 17 handlers of Decision 27, but it has the same ownership retry and the same check in the same place, unchanged since before rc9 (commit 40bf6a8, no change between rc8 and rc9), so it is a tenth handler whose check no test reaches, for the reason of group (2); the end of the try block and of the catch of the retry (lines 64 and 75) run only when the retry succeeds, and it cannot.
ResidualRisk: Low: the catch is one WriteError and continue, the shape that the covered siblings assert. A later command that threw for exactly the RestoreOwnerError record of a getter would be reported as a ReadSecurityError of the item and the loop would go on, as it did before rc9 for all 17 handlers; no state of an item gets a getter there.
RelatedTests: PipelineControl.Tests (the later command that throws, the eight handlers that can be driven there); Access.Tests, ParameterSets.Access.Tests, Inheritance.Tests: the read errors and the retry of the getters.

WhyNotTested: The closure re-reads the item inside InvokeAsOwner. InvokeAsOwner reads the owner first, which needs the same READ_CONTROL right as the read that failed, so the retry stops before the closure runs; the documentation and PathErrors assert the resulting ReadSecurityError. A DACL that denies reading the DACL but not the owner cannot be built.
ResidualRisk: None found: the closure repeats the first attempt.
RelatedTests: PathErrors: An item whose owner may not read its permissions.

WhyNotTested: EffectiveAccess.GetEffectiveAccess hides every failure of its Authz calls in a result with OperationFailed, which the cmdlet turns into GetEffectiveAccessError. The catch (Exception) blocks and the InvokeAsOwner retry therefore see an exception only from what runs outside those calls: the read of the descriptor of the item (EffectiveAccess.cs, the FileSystemInfo overload) or the conversion of the account. The only local failure of the descriptor read is access denied, which the UnauthorizedAccessException branch handles and the tests cover; no other local trigger was found, and the unresolved identity, which the conversion accepts, ends in OperationFailed.
ResidualRisk: Low: a failure of the descriptor read other than access denied, such as an I/O error of the volume, would run the unvisited catch, which writes one ReadEffectivePermissionError and continues like its tested siblings.
RelatedTests: Access.Tests: unresolved identity for a path and a descriptor, remote fallback, privilege warnings.

WhyNotTested: The unvisited points are the catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) of an audit write, its InvokeAsOwner retry and the closure of that retry. Local NTFS never raises that exception for an audit change: as a basic user all seven audit cmdlets get an IOException, error 1314 (A required privilege is not held), in both editions (probe); with the Security privilege nothing in a DACL can deny the privilege-only right, and a loopback administrative share ended in no exception for all five either (probe, elevated, EnablePrivileges on and off). The retry is the InvokeAsOwner code that the access cmdlets share, so its success, failure and RestoreOwnerError paths run there; only the audit closure bodies, which repeat the first attempt, are unexecuted. Since rc9 the catch of the retry also holds the check IsFromLaterCommand(ex2) with a rethrow (Decision 27, item 7); it sits inside the catch that no run reaches, and an audit write does not depend on the DACL, so the action never fails first and the retry never starts (Decision 27: this is why the five audit handlers have no test of the check).
ResidualRisk: Low to medium: an audit write that a file server answers with access denied runs lines that no test reaches. The instrumented live suite (the first lab and three matrix cells, both editions, all roles) runs the audit cmdlets over SMB and visits none of these points: the account without the Security privilege on the file server gets an IOException with error 1314, and a probe of eight audit calls against shares with Full, Change, and Read share permissions, as an administrator of the file server, raised no error in either edition.
RelatedTests: PathErrors (denied write and ownership retry for the access cmdlets), FileHash and SecurityDescriptor tests (ownership retry), Audit.Tests (privilege missing or disabled).

WhyNotTested: The unvisited points are the last catch (Exception) of the per-item loop, taken when the DACL API fails with anything but access denied after the item was found. A read or write of the DACL on local NTFS either succeeds or fails with access denied (covered), and the probes found no other failure for these cmdlets: an unresolvable SID is accepted, a locked file does not matter because the security APIs ignore share modes, and a dangling junction is read as the link itself. One input does trigger that catch, a deny entry without rights, which .NET refuses with an ArgumentException; Add-NTFSAccess, Remove-NTFSAccess and Add-NTFSAudit take it and are tested (an Allow entry without rights is accepted, because the module adds Synchronize to it).         A cmdlet that has no rights parameter, such as the read and inheritance cmdlets, has no such input. A second trigger exists for the cmdlets that add entries: an ACL that is full. In both editions the 1,818th entry that was added to a security descriptor in memory, with -SecurityDescriptor, raised an OverflowException, "Length of the access control list exceed the allowed maximum" (probe p37: unresolvable SIDs with ReadData; 1,816 entries were written and read back without an error, and one more added with -Path succeeded, so the overflow itself was not run with -Path). By reading the source, the -Path loop takes that exception in the same handler as the zero-mask case, whereas the -SecurityDescriptor sets have no handler around the add, so there the exception ends the cmdlet. It was not turned into a test of its own. A volume without ACL support or a corrupt descriptor cannot be created safely on the shared host.

The catches of the cmdlets that only read or change inheritance have no known trigger. A catch that wraps the write of the result is entered also when a later command raises something while it takes the object; every catch-all whose try block writes directly passes that exception on (a scan of the source finds no exception; it cannot see a write inside a helper such as the owner restore of InvokeAsOwner, an accepted limitation), and the PipelineControl tests run that part for every cmdlet.
RelatedTests: Access.Tests and Audit.Tests: a deny or audit entry without rights for Add-NTFSAccess, Remove-NTFSAccess and Add-NTFSAudit (AddAceError and RemoveAceError, ArgumentException, WriteError, target, continuation, nothing written). WhyNotTested: The unvisited points are the catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) of an audit write, its InvokeAsOwner retry and the closure of that retry. Local NTFS never raises that exception for an audit change: as a basic user all seven audit cmdlets get an IOException, error 1314 (A required privilege is not held), in both editions (probe); with the Security privilege nothing in a DACL can deny the privilege-only right, and a loopback administrative share ended in no exception for all five either (probe, elevated, EnablePrivileges on and off). The retry is the InvokeAsOwner code that the access cmdlets share, so its success, failure and RestoreOwnerError paths run there; only the audit closure bodies, which repeat the first attempt, are unexecuted. Since rc9 the catch of the retry also holds the check IsFromLaterCommand(ex2) with a rethrow (Decision 27, item 7); it sits inside the catch that no run reaches, and an audit write does not depend on the DACL, so the action never fails first and the retry never starts (Decision 27: this is why the five audit handlers have no test of the check).
ResidualRisk: Low to medium: an audit write that a file server answers with access denied runs lines that no test reaches. The instrumented live suite (the first lab and three matrix cells, both editions, all roles) runs the audit cmdlets over SMB and visits none of these points: the account without the Security privilege on the file server gets an IOException with error 1314, and a probe of eight audit calls against shares with Full, Change, and Read share permissions, as an administrator of the file server, raised no error in either edition.
RelatedTests: PathErrors (denied write and ownership retry for the access cmdlets), FileHash and SecurityDescriptor tests (ownership retry), Audit.Tests (privilege missing or disabled).

WhyNotTested: Four groups of points. (1) The last catch (Exception) of the per-item loop, taken when the read fails with anything but access denied after the item was found: a read of the descriptor on local NTFS either succeeds or fails with access denied (covered), and the probes found no other failure (the explanation of ACCESS-GENERIC-CATCH and EFFECTIVE-ACCESS-CATCH of the 2026-10-10 report, unchanged). (2) Since rc9 (Decision 27, item 7) the catch of the ownership retry holds the check IsFromLaterCommand(ex2) with a rethrow. The rethrow runs only when a later command throws for the RestoreOwnerError record that InvokeAsOwner writes while it gives the owner back. InvokeAsOwner starts with FileSystemOwner.GetOwner, which needs the READ_CONTROL right whose denial started the retry, so the retry of a getter ends at that first statement with a ReadSecurityError and never reaches the restore: no state of an item takes a getter to the rethrow, with a local volume or a share (Decision 27, item 7: 9 of the 17 handlers have no test for this reason, the audit cmdlets for the reason of AUDIT-OWNER-RETRY). The check is the same IsFromLaterCommand call that the eight handlers with a test run. (3) GetInheritance only: the guards if (inheritanceInfo != null), in the loop of the paths and in the loop of the descriptors. Both overloads of FileSystemInheritanceInfo.GetFileSystemInheritanceInfo end in return new, so the else side of the guards has no input. (4) GetSecurityDescriptor only: it is not one of the 17 handlers of Decision 27, but it has the same ownership retry and the same check in the same place, unchanged since before rc9 (commit 40bf6a8, no change between rc8 and rc9), so it is a tenth handler whose check no test reaches, for the reason of group (2); the end of the try block and of the catch of the retry (lines 64 and 75) run only when the retry succeeds, and it cannot.
ResidualRisk: Low: the catch is one WriteError and continue, the shape that the covered siblings assert. A later command that threw for exactly the RestoreOwnerError record of a getter would be reported as a ReadSecurityError of the item and the loop would go on, as it did before rc9 for all 17 handlers; no state of an item gets a getter there.
RelatedTests: PipelineControl.Tests (the later command that throws, the eight handlers that can be driven there); Access.Tests, ParameterSets.Access.Tests, Inheritance.Tests: the read errors and the retry of the getters.

WhyNotTested: The closure re-reads the item inside InvokeAsOwner. InvokeAsOwner reads the owner first, which needs the same READ_CONTROL right as the read that failed, so the retry stops before the closure runs; the documentation and PathErrors assert the resulting ReadSecurityError. A DACL that denies reading the DACL but not the owner cannot be built.
ResidualRisk: None found: the closure repeats the first attempt.
RelatedTests: PathErrors: An item whose owner may not read its permissions.

WhyNotTested: The unvisited points are the last catch (Exception) of the per-item loop, taken when the DACL API fails with anything but access denied after the item was found. A read or write of the DACL on local NTFS either succeeds or fails with access denied (covered), and the probes found no other failure for these cmdlets: an unresolvable SID is accepted, a locked file does not matter because the security APIs ignore share modes, and a dangling junction is read as the link itself. One input does trigger that catch, a deny entry without rights, which .NET refuses with an ArgumentException; Add-NTFSAccess, Remove-NTFSAccess and Add-NTFSAudit take it and are tested (an Allow entry without rights is accepted, because the module adds Synchronize to it).         A cmdlet that has no rights parameter, such as the read and inheritance cmdlets, has no such input. A second trigger exists for the cmdlets that add entries: an ACL that is full. In both editions the 1,818th entry that was added to a security descriptor in memory, with -SecurityDescriptor, raised an OverflowException, "Length of the access control list exceed the allowed maximum" (probe p37: unresolvable SIDs with ReadData; 1,816 entries were written and read back without an error, and one more added with -Path succeeded, so the overflow itself was not run with -Path). By reading the source, the -Path loop takes that exception in the same handler as the zero-mask case, whereas the -SecurityDescriptor sets have no handler around the add, so there the exception ends the cmdlet. It was not turned into a test of its own. A volume without ACL support or a corrupt descriptor cannot be created safely on the shared host.
ResidualRisk: Low: one WriteError(exception, id, category, path) and continue, the shape that the access-denied and ReadFileError siblings of the same loops assert and that the zero-mask tests assert for the cmdlets that add and remove entries. The catches of the cmdlets that only read or change inheritance have no known trigger. A catch that wraps the write of the result is entered also when a later command raises something while it takes the object; every catch-all whose try block writes directly passes that exception on (a scan of the source finds no exception; it cannot see a write inside a helper such as the owner restore of InvokeAsOwner, an accepted limitation), and the PipelineControl tests run that part for every cmdlet.
RelatedTests: Access.Tests and Audit.Tests: a deny or audit entry without rights for Add-NTFSAccess, Remove-NTFSAccess and Add-NTFSAudit (AddAceError and RemoveAceError, ArgumentException, WriteError, target, continuation, nothing written). PathErrors: ReadFileError, ReadSecurityError, denied write and ownership retry, each with continuation. WhyNotTested: Four groups of points. (1) The last catch (Exception) of the per-item loop, taken when the read fails with anything but access denied after the item was found: a read of the descriptor on local NTFS either succeeds or fails with access denied (covered), and the probes found no other failure (the explanation of ACCESS-GENERIC-CATCH and EFFECTIVE-ACCESS-CATCH of the 2026-10-10 report, unchanged). (2) Since rc9 (Decision 27, item 7) the catch of the ownership retry holds the check IsFromLaterCommand(ex2) with a rethrow. The rethrow runs only when a later command throws for the RestoreOwnerError record that InvokeAsOwner writes while it gives the owner back. InvokeAsOwner starts with FileSystemOwner.GetOwner, which needs the READ_CONTROL right whose denial started the retry, so the retry of a getter ends at that first statement with a ReadSecurityError and never reaches the restore: no state of an item takes a getter to the rethrow, with a local volume or a share (Decision 27, item 7: 9 of the 17 handlers have no test for this reason, the audit cmdlets for the reason of AUDIT-OWNER-RETRY). The check is the same IsFromLaterCommand call that the eight handlers with a test run. (3) GetInheritance only: the guards if (inheritanceInfo != null), in the loop of the paths and in the loop of the descriptors. Both overloads of FileSystemInheritanceInfo.GetFileSystemInheritanceInfo end in return new, so the else side of the guards has no input. (4) GetSecurityDescriptor only: it is not one of the 17 handlers of Decision 27, but it has the same ownership retry and the same check in the same place, unchanged since before rc9 (commit 40bf6a8, no change between rc8 and rc9), so it is a tenth handler whose check no test reaches, for the reason of group (2); the end of the try block and of the catch of the retry (lines 64 and 75) run only when the retry succeeds, and it cannot.
ResidualRisk: Low: the catch is one WriteError and continue, the shape that the covered siblings assert. A later command that threw for exactly the RestoreOwnerError record of a getter would be reported as a ReadSecurityError of the item and the loop would go on, as it did before rc9 for all 17 handlers; no state of an item gets a getter there.
RelatedTests: PipelineControl.Tests (the later command that throws, the eight handlers that can be driven there); Access.Tests, ParameterSets.Access.Tests, Inheritance.Tests: the read errors and the retry of the getters.

WhyNotTested: The access twin is tested: a NULL DACL, which Windows reads as an ACL with no entries and .NET reports as one entry for Everyone, runs the branch where the list of sources is empty (Access.Tests). The unvisited branch that remains is the second operand of getInheritedFrom && inheritedFrom.Count > 0 in the audit twin. GetInheritedFrom returns one source for each entry of the SACL that it reads, also for the fallback text of an unknown parent, and an empty list only for a descriptor without a SACL. The loop that holds the condition runs over the audit entries of the same SACL, so an empty list means that the loop has no entry and does not run, as for every item without a SACL (Audit.Tests: the item has no SACL). The setting that turns the lookup off and the fallback cover the other outcomes. A probe shows that an integrity label in the SACL of a folder is not part of the SACL that the module reads, so the sources of the audit entries stay aligned with the entries (probe, both editions).
ResidualRisk: Low: the two lists are aligned by position, which assumes that the .NET API returns a rule for every entry of the ACL that Windows names a source for; an entry type that it skips would shift the sources. No such entry was found on NTFS, and none was tested.
RelatedTests: Access.Tests: InheritedFrom with the setting on and off, for an unknown parent and for a NULL DACL; Audit.Tests: InheritedFrom of audit entries and an item without a SACL; ObjectApis.Tests: an empty DACL.

WhyNotTested: The unvisited branch point is the arm of if (error != 0) in GetEffectivePermissions_AuthzAccessCheck that is taken when AuthzAccessCheck returns false and the last Win32 error is 0. A failing call sets an error code: the call that fails for an unresolved identity takes the other arm, throws, and is tested (the cmdlet writes GetEffectiveAccessError; since 5.0.0-rc8, 25fe775, also for what the initialization of the resource manager throws). No input makes the call return false without an error, and a test cannot make the Authz service fail on the shared host.
ResidualRisk: Low: a false return without an error code would not be thrown, and the granted access would be read from a buffer that the call did not fill; the documentation of AuthzAccessCheck names an error code for every failure.
RelatedTests: Access.Tests: an unresolved identity, a computer that cannot be reached, names of this computer, an empty name.

WhyNotTested: The fallback of fdd7a8b: a computer in a domain offers the remote interface of its authorization manager to every caller and answers only its administrators and the members of Access Control Assistance Operators, so the context for a caller who is neither gets access denied, and for a name of this computer the cmdlet then asks the local manager. It needs a domain member and a caller who is not an administrator there, which the host is not. The live tests run it: the role ServerAdmin (an account that is not an administrator of the client) calls Get-NTFSEffectiveAccess without -ServerName and with the name of the client; so does the unit suite as a basic user on a domain member (OSFile25, both editions). What no run visits is the branch for the answer RPC server unavailable of the context initialization, which does not throw: it needs a remote computer that answers the initialization of the resource manager and stops answering before the context is made.
ResidualRisk: Low for the fallback (the live tests and the unit suite on a domain member visit it, Stage B of the report); the throw of another error ends in the catch of the cmdlet as GetEffectiveAccessError.
RelatedTests: Live tests: Get-NTFSEffectiveAccess for a domain account as an account that is not an administrator of the client (role ServerAdmin, 2 tests); Access.Tests: a name of this computer as a basic user on a domain member (the unit suite of the matrix).

The throw for another error is visited since the tests-only round: a name of 40,000 characters, which Windows rejects with another error, ends there (Access.Tests: When Windows rejects the name of -ServerName), and since 5.0.0-rc8 (25fe775) the catch of GetEffectivePermissions hands the exception to the cmdlet as GetEffectiveAccessError. The empty name, a space, backslashes, a colon, a bracket, 300 characters, malformed and well-formed addresses never produce that error (probe).
